assumptions: Preview and final both use the published 720p Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash rate. Google says a draft can be 360p, and it does not publish a separate 360p price.
Each shot is quoted as two takes: one preview and one final.
The retake reserve is one extra preview of every priced shot. That is not a published fee. It counts against the production allocation.

A Gemini Omni clip shorter than 3 seconds is quoted at 3 seconds, and a clip longer than 15 seconds is split. Google publishes one-second lengths from 3 to 15. Shaping the call that way is an assumption.
Still frames are not priced. This card has no still-image rate, so the art-director line stays at $0.
Sound is not priced. This card has no audio-only rate, so the sound-designer line stays at $0.
Dailies review does not call a paid model in this build, so the review itself is $0. A retake is estimated as one preview and checked against the fix-loop line. It is not spent here.
The fix-loop reserve is the locked fix-loop allocation when the split has one. It is not a new price. If the split has no fix-loop line, the reserve is $0.
Color and mix are not priced. This card has no grade or mix rate, so a paid color or mix call is unknown. This build does not make one.
Delivery is not priced. This card has no packaging rate, so a paid delivery call is unknown. This build does not make one.
A generator row may name a provider and an endpoint. Those are call addresses already stored in config/model-routing.json. They are not prices. A row without an endpoint cannot be called live.
Audio, color, and delivery still have no published dollar amount in this repo. A live call for one of those is refused until a per-call price override is approved.

Seedance 2.0 and Seedance 2.0 fast accept duration auto, or a whole number of seconds from 4 to 15. A shot is rounded up to the next allowed second and quoted at that length. The rule was read from the fal API pages on 2026-11-12. Fast accepts 480p and 720p. Seedance 2.0 also accepts 1080p and 4k. This row still prices 720p.

Kling 4.0 on fal accepts a whole number of seconds from 3 to 30, at 720p or 1080p. That duration rule was read from the fal text-to-video page on 2026-11-12. The row still has no endpoint, so a live call is refused. The per-shot multi-prompt minimum of 1 second is not the rule for this row.
Gemini Omni's 3 to 15 second quote is still an assumption. Whole seconds were not verified for that model, so a length inside that range is not rounded.
